title: Basic Troubleshooting
summary: What happens when your circuit doesn't work?

steps.title: Basic Troubleshooting
steps.markdownContent:
What happens when your circuit doesn't work? Don't worry—every engineer runs into bugs! You just need to become an **Engineering Detective**! 🕵️

### The 3 Clues to Check:
1. **Check Power**: Is the little green light labeled **'ON'** lit on the Arduino? If not, check if the USB cable is firmly plugged in.
2. **Check the Pin Match**: Look at your code. Did the code command **Pin 13**, but the wire is plugged into **Pin 12**? If the pins don't match, the signal won't reach your part!
3. **Check Ground (GND)**: Is the ground wire securely plugged in? Remember, electricity can't flow without a complete return path.

Take on the troubleshooting mission below: find the mismatched pin and fix the circuit!

quickCheck.question: If an LED light does not turn on, what is the best first thing to check?
options: Check that wires are plugged into the right pins and firmly connected
Throw all the parts into the trash
Paint the wires with colorful glitter
quickCheck.explanation: Checking that wires are firmly connected to the correct pins fixes most electronics puzzles!
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: When something doesn't work, stay calm and check connections first: are wires in the right spots?

quickCheck.question: If your code commands Pin 13, but your wire is plugged into Pin 8, what will happen?
options: The part on Pin 8 will not receive the command
The computer will turn into a pumpkin
Pin 8 will automatically slide over to Pin 13
quickCheck.explanation: Code commands specific pins! If the wire is plugged into the wrong pin, the signal won't reach it.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Code and wires must match! If code commands Pin 13, the wire must be connected to Pin 13.
